# core/tls13server.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/tls13server.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

The server side of TLS 1.3, with no input or
output of its own, like core/tls13client: the caller passes the bytes that
arrived to `tls13s_feed` and writes what it appends to `out`.

It answers a ClientHello that offers TLS 1.3, one of the three suites
(TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384,
TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256) and an X25519 key share, with the
certificate chain the caller gives and a CertificateVerify signed with
its key: ECDSA P-256 (ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256) or RSA
(rsa_pss_rsae_sha256). It reads the server name the client asks for and
picks an application protocol (ALPN) from the server's list. The state is
a `Tls13Client` (the record layer and the key schedule are the same); the
server reads with its `c_*` keys and writes with its `s_*` keys.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, and the keys
have the lengths the record layer needs, whatever the client sends. Not
proved: that the protocol is followed (tests/tls.sh runs OpenSSL's client
against it). Not done: HelloRetryRequest (a client that sends no X25519
share is refused), client certificates, session tickets and early data.

`import "core/tls13server.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/sha256.bastio](core-sha256.md), [core/sha512.bastio](core-sha512.md), [core/hkdf.bastio](core-hkdf.md), [core/tls13.bastio](core-tls13.md), [core/tls13hs.bastio](core-tls13hs.md), [core/aes.bastio](core-aes.md), [core/aesgcm.bastio](core-aesgcm.md), [core/chacha20.bastio](core-chacha20.md), [core/poly1305.bastio](core-poly1305.md), [core/chacha20poly1305.bastio](core-chacha20poly1305.md), [core/tls13record.bastio](core-tls13record.md), [core/x25519.bastio](core-x25519.md), [core/der.bastio](core-der.md), [core/ed25519.bastio](core-ed25519.md), [core/p256.bastio](core-p256.md), [core/p384.bastio](core-p384.md), [core/rsa.bastio](core-rsa.md), [core/x509.bastio](core-x509.md), [core/tls13client.bastio](core-tls13client.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`tls13s_new`](#tls13s_new) | Starts a server connection. |
| [`tls13s_name`](#tls13s_name) | The server name the client asked for (a copy; empty if it sent none). |
| [`tls13s_feed`](#tls13s_feed) | Gives the server the bytes `data` that arrived from the client. |

## Types and constants

### `Tls13sHello`

```bastio
struct Tls13sHello { suite: u64, sid: Bytes, share: Bytes, name: Bytes, protocols: Bytes, scheme: u64, v13: bool }
```

Internal: the ClientHello fields the server needs.

## Functions

### `tls13s_new`

```bastio
fn tls13s_new(random: &Bytes, priv_key: &Bytes, nonce: &Bytes, chain: &Bytes, kind: u64, ka: &Bytes, kb: &Bytes, alpn: &Bytes) -> Tls13Client
  requires blen(random) == 32 && blen(priv_key) == 32 && blen(nonce) == 32 && blen(chain) < 1048576
  requires blen(ka) < 65536 && blen(kb) < 65536 && blen(alpn) <= 256 && (kind == 1 || kind == 2)
  ensures tls13c_ok(result) && result.state == 0
```

Starts a server connection. `random`, `priv_key` (the X25519 key) and
`nonce` (for the signature: the ECDSA nonce or the PSS salt) are 32 bytes
each that nobody can predict, used once. `chain` is the server's
certificate chain as DER certificates one after the other, its own first.
`kind` is the kind of key that signs: 1 RSA, with the modulus `ka` and the
private exponent `kb` (big-endian), or 2 ECDSA P-256, with the 32-byte
scalar `ka`. `alpn` is the list of protocols the server speaks, in its
order of preference, in the form of the ALPN extension's contents (each
name behind a one-byte length). Nothing is sent before the ClientHello.

Example:

```bastio
let r = balloc(32);
let k = balloc(32);
let nonce = balloc(32);
let chain = balloc(0);
let d = balloc(32);
let none = balloc(0);
let alpn = balloc(0);
let s = tls13s_new(r, k, nonce, chain, 2, d, none, alpn);
let st = tls13c_state(s);
tls13c_free(s);
bfree(alpn);
bfree(none);
bfree(d);
bfree(chain);
bfree(nonce);
bfree(k);
bfree(r);
if st != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13s_name`

```bastio
fn tls13s_name(c: &Tls13Client) -> Bytes
```

The server name the client asked for (a copy; empty if it sent none).

Example:

```bastio
let c = tls13c_blank();
let n = tls13s_name(c);
let l = blen(n);
bfree(n);
tls13c_free(c);
if l != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13s_feed`

```bastio
fn tls13s_feed(c: &mut Tls13Client, data: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8], app: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(data) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Gives the server the bytes `data` that arrived from the client. What the
server sends in answer is appended to `out`, the client's application
data to `app`. Returns 0, or an error code once the connection has failed
(state 7): 1 malformed, 2 unexpected message, 3 nothing in common with
the ClientHello (TLS 1.3, a suite, an X25519 share, a signature scheme for
the key), 4 bad key exchange, 5 decryption failed, 7 the key or the chain
cannot be used, 8 bad Finished, 9 alert from the client.

Example:

```bastio
let r = balloc(32);
let k = balloc(32);
let nonce = balloc(32);
let chain = balloc(0);
let d = balloc(32);
let none = balloc(0);
let alpn = balloc(0);
let mut s = tls13s_new(r, k, nonce, chain, 2, d, none, alpn);
let mut out = text_new();
let mut app = text_new();
let junk = bfrom("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n");
let code = tls13s_feed(&mut s, junk, &mut out, &mut app);
let st = tls13c_state(s);
bfree(junk);
vec_free(app);
vec_free(out);
tls13c_free(s);
bfree(alpn);
bfree(none);
bfree(d);
bfree(chain);
bfree(nonce);
bfree(k);
bfree(r);
if code == 0 || st != 7 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13s_send`

```bastio
fn tls13s_send(c: &mut Tls13Client, data: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> bool
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(data) < 1073741824
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Seals `data` as application data records from the server and appends
them to `out`. False unless the handshake is complete.

Example:

```bastio
let c = tls13c_blank();
let mut out = text_new();
let data = bfrom("hello");
let mut s = c;
let sent = tls13c_check(s) && tls13s_send(&mut s, data, &mut out);
bfree(data);
vec_free(out);
tls13c_free(s);
if sent { return 1; }
```

### `tls13s_shutdown`

```bastio
fn tls13s_shutdown(c: &mut Tls13Client, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> bool
  requires tls13c_ok(c)
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Appends a close_notify alert from the server to `out`; the server sends
nothing more but still reads what the client sends until it closes too
(state 6). False unless the handshake is complete (or it was already shut).

Example:

```bastio
let mut c = tls13c_blank();
let mut out = text_new();
let shut = tls13c_check(c) && tls13s_shutdown(&mut c, &mut out);
vec_free(out);
tls13c_free(c);
if shut { return 1; }
```

### `tls13s_is_server`

```bastio
fn tls13s_is_server(c: &Tls13Client) -> bool
```

Whether `c` is the server side of a connection (made by `tls13s_new`).

Example:

```bastio
let c = tls13c_blank();
let s = tls13s_is_server(c);
tls13c_free(c);
if s { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `tls13s_push_u24`

```bastio
fn tls13s_push_u24(t: &mut Vec[u8], v: u64)
  requires v < 16777216
  ensures vlen(t) == vlen(old(t)) + 3
```

Internal: appends the 24-bit big-endian number `v` to `t`.

### `tls13s_wrap`

```bastio
fn tls13s_wrap(ty: u8, body: Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(body) < 16777216
  ensures blen(result) == blen(body) + 4
```

Internal: the handshake message of type `ty` with the contents `body`.

### `tls13s_plain`

```bastio
fn tls13s_plain(out: &mut Vec[u8], ty: u8, body: &Bytes)
  requires blen(body) <= 16384
```

Internal: appends a plain record of type `ty` (version 0x0303) around `body`.

### `tls13s_send_record`

```bastio
fn tls13s_send_record(c: &mut Tls13Client, ty: u8, plain: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> bool
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(plain) <= 16384
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: appends a record of type `ty` carrying `plain`, sealed with the
server's keys, to `out`.

### `tls13s_send_message`

```bastio
fn tls13s_send_message(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> bool
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: adds the handshake message `msg` to the transcript and sends
it, sealed, in as many records as it takes.

### `tls13s_der_len`

```bastio
fn tls13s_der_len(b: &Bytes, at: u64) -> u64
  requires at <= blen(b)
  ensures result == 0 || (result >= 2 && result <= blen(b) - at)
```

Internal: the length of the DER element at `b[at..]` with its header, or
0 when it is not a SEQUENCE that fits.

### `tls13s_certificate`

```bastio
fn tls13s_certificate(chain: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires blen(chain) < 1048576
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) < 8388608
```

Internal: the Certificate message for the DER certificates `chain`, or
None when they do not split into certificates.

### `tls13s_der_int`

```bastio
fn tls13s_der_int(t: &mut Vec[u8], b: &Bytes, from: u64)
  requires from + 32 <= blen(b)
  ensures vlen(t) <= vlen(old(t)) + 35
```

Internal: appends the DER INTEGER for the 32-byte big-endian number at
`b[from..from+32]`.

### `tls13s_sign`

```bastio
fn tls13s_sign(c: &Tls13Client, h: &Bytes, scheme: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && (blen(h) == 32 || blen(h) == 48)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) <= 512
```

Internal: the signature of the server's key over the CertificateVerify
contents for the transcript hash `h`, and the scheme, or None.

### `tls13s_hello_free`

```bastio
fn tls13s_hello_free(h: Tls13sHello)
```

Internal: frees what `tls13s_parse_hello` returned.

### `tls13s_extensions`

```bastio
fn tls13s_extensions(msg: &Bytes, at: u64, h: &mut Tls13sHello, kind: u64) -> bool
  requires at <= blen(msg) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures blen(h.share) == 32 || blen(h.share) == 0
  ensures blen(h.name) <= 255 && blen(h.protocols) < 65536 && blen(h.sid) <= 32
  ensures h.scheme == 0 || h.scheme == 1027 || h.scheme == 2052
  requires (blen(h.share) == 32 || blen(h.share) == 0) && blen(h.name) <= 255 && blen(h.protocols) < 65536 && blen(h.sid) <= 32
  requires h.scheme == 0 || h.scheme == 1027 || h.scheme == 2052
```

Internal: reads the extensions of a ClientHello `msg[at..]` into `h`.
False when they are malformed.

### `tls13s_parse_hello`

```bastio
fn tls13s_parse_hello(msg: &Bytes, kind: u64) -> Option[Tls13sHello]
  requires blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> (blen(result.Some.sid) <= 32 && (blen(result.Some.share) == 32 || blen(result.Some.share) == 0))
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> (blen(result.Some.name) <= 255 && blen(result.Some.protocols) < 65536)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> (result.Some.suite == 4865 || result.Some.suite == 4866 || result.Some.suite == 4867 || result.Some.suite == 0)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> (result.Some.scheme == 0 || result.Some.scheme == 1027 || result.Some.scheme == 2052)
```

Internal: the fields of the ClientHello `msg`, or None when it is
malformed.

### `tls13s_pick_protocol`

```bastio
fn tls13s_pick_protocol(mine: &Bytes, theirs: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  ensures blen(result) <= 255
```

Internal: the first protocol of the server's list `mine` that the client
offered in `theirs` (empty if none).

### `tls13s_server_hello`

```bastio
fn tls13s_server_hello(h: &Tls13sHello, random: &Bytes, pubkey: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(h.sid) <= 32 && h.suite < 65536 && blen(random) <= 32 && blen(pubkey) == 32
  ensures blen(result) < 200
```

Internal: the ServerHello for the hello `h`, with the server's random
`random` and key share `pubkey`.

### `tls13s_encrypted_extensions`

```bastio
fn tls13s_encrypted_extensions(proto: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(proto) <= 255
  ensures blen(result) < 300
```

Internal: the EncryptedExtensions, with the chosen protocol if any.

### `tls13s_client_hello`

```bastio
fn tls13s_client_hello(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: handles the ClientHello `msg` (state 0): sends the server's
whole flight and waits for the client's Finished (state 4).

### `tls13s_finished`

```bastio
fn tls13s_finished(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: handles the client's Finished `msg` (state 4).

### `tls13s_after`

```bastio
fn tls13s_after(c: &mut Tls13Client, msg: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(msg) < 1048576
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: handles a handshake message after the handshake (state 5): a
KeyUpdate changes the client's keys, and the server's if asked.

### `tls13s_handshake_data`

```bastio
fn tls13s_handshake_data(c: &mut Tls13Client, plain: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(plain) <= 16640
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: joins the handshake bytes `plain` to what is left of earlier
ones and handles the whole messages.

### `tls13s_record`

```bastio
fn tls13s_record(c: &mut Tls13Client, rec: &Bytes, out: &mut Vec[u8], app: &mut Vec[u8]) -> u64
  requires tls13c_ok(c) && blen(rec) >= 5 && blen(rec) <= 16645
  ensures tls13c_ok(c)
```

Internal: handles one whole record `rec` (with its header).
